description: Susdrain, the sustainable drainage community run by CIRIA, publishes a collection of case studies of sustainable drainage systems (SuDS) in the United Kingdom, from house and garden retrofits and supermarket car parks to housing estates, schools, health centres and public spaces. The list can be filtered alphabetically and by SuDS component type, such as rainwater harvesting, green roofs, permeable paving, swales and conveyance channels, filtration and infiltration components, geocellular storage, detention basins, and inlets, outlets and control structures. Many case studies are peer reviewed, some are award submissions, and newer "light" case studies are marked as not peer reviewed. The collection is free to read online; no licence is stated for reuse. Caveats: the page itself says the extent to which each scheme follows SuDS principles varies with the guidance, client brief and design criteria of its time, and the case studies are descriptive pages, not a structured dataset. Coverage is mainly the United Kingdom. It supports design and evidence gathering for green and blue drainage infrastructure and flood risk reduction; the related record is the CIRIA SuDS Manual C753.
